ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Orthopedic radiograph interpretation: 5

A trauma radiograph shows subtle bone findings but also a joint effusion and nearby soft-tissue gas. The clinician includes these in the interpretation rather than reading only cortical lines. Which systematic review principle is illustrated?

  1. Assess extension into the joint surface
  2. Inspect soft tissues as well as bone
  3. Obtain adequate orthogonal views
  4. Include adjacent joints when indicated
  5. Describe distal-fragment position relative to the proximal fragment
Answer and explanation

Inspect soft tissues as well as bone

Gas, swelling, effusion and foreign bodies can provide important injury clues.

Option explanations

Inspect soft tissues as well as bone: Gas, swelling, effusion and foreign bodies can provide important injury clues.

Obtain adequate orthogonal views: A fracture or displacement can be missed or mischaracterized on a single projection. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Include adjacent joints when indicated: Shaft injuries may be accompanied by proximal or distal joint disruption. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Describe distal-fragment position relative to the proximal fragment: Standard descriptions use the distal fragment relative to the proximal fragment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Assess extension into the joint surface: Articular involvement affects congruity, prognosis and treatment planning. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
